parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a hostile national border and facilities regime onto a hostile division. The Feb-2025 cable lets officers refuse entry where documents cast doubt on sex, with fraud referral (lifetime ineligibility) considered. Federal and division laws bar trans people from single-sex facilities; a trespass statute produced a documented March-2025 arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward. A 2017 religious-liberties statute licenses service refusal; the division has no gender-identity nondiscrimination law and its supreme court ruled 8-1 against a trans minor. If detained nationally, immigration-custody abuse and a corrections conversion-therapy policy apply. Counterweights: violence is near baseline (last killing 2017, 49-year federal hate-crime sentence), 67-68% public support for protections, and active litigation. Universal document/facility exposure with criminal tail and thin state recourse places this in Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable: document discrepancy or other doubt about sex -> refuse the case; suspected wilful misrepresentation considered for permanent fraud ineligibility; X markers discontinued; 8+ foreign governments issued trans travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, never automatic, limited waiver; civil-liberties suit pending; litigation may shift which rules bind at travel time.
entry_documents.interaction: Visa refusal -> removal/stranding; possible secondary screening and detention feeding into birth-sex custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented March 2025 trespass arrest, 24 hours held in the men's ward; national corrections conversion-therapy policy (hormones cut, hair shorn); immigration custody abuse: forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; name changes barred in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release granted; national hate-crime statute used successfully (49-year sentence, 2017); consular/legal-aid channels not documented as blocked for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility ejection -> trespass arrest -> birth-sex ward placement; entry refusal -> immigration custody exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; division's May 2024 birth-sex bathroom law for public schools; 4 states criminalize facility use (trespass, up to 60 days); division graded 'Worst Laws' July 2026; March 2026 licence-marker ban.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states have no mapped ban; four municipal nondiscrimination ordinances; two restrictive bills died in 2024.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor in capitols, courthouses, parks or schools risks ejection or arrest if asked to depart and refusing.

care_services.exposure: 2017 religious-liberties statute gives providers a statutory basis to refuse service on birth-sex belief; under-18 care banned (2023); adolescent gender clinic closed; no state gender-identity nondiscrimination law.
care_services.protection: Not documented. No traveler-facing adult care-access protection appears; national health-rule challenges pending.
care_services.interaction: Traveling minor needing hormones or an adult needing emergency care could meet refusal with no state-level remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State supreme court called a trans boy a 'minor female' (2025); division in the 'legislatively erased' tier; national orders describe care as 'mutilation'; May 2026 counterterrorism framing of 'radically pro-transgender' groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 67-68% public support for nondiscrimination laws; several national orders blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises arrest and refusal risk at encounters; society polls markedly more accepting than law.

minors_guardians.exposure: April 2025 8-1 denial of a trans minor's name change; 2023 care ban; school sports ban requiring genital/DNA verification; national order criminalizing teachers facilitating social transition; DOJ subpoenas of youth records.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented for visitors; even a consent-based parental petition was denied.
minors_guardians.interaction: Trans teen travelling alone or with a trans guardian faces care denial, hostile judicial posture, and no local remedy.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Last documented bias-motivated killing of a trans person in the division: 2017; trans homicide 6.6/100k vs 6.0 general population (2008-2025) - near background, not a campaign; no documented pattern against visitors.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Working federal hate-crime prosecution (49-year sentence); 3,000-person pride parade; 2019 and 2024 polls show 67-68% support for protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public attitudes are more accepting than statute; bias violence draws national prosecution rather than impunity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state gender-identity nondiscrimination law; 1994 hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; no enforcement data on adult facility application; March 2026 licence-law exceptions unsourced; litigation unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Passport suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; four municipal ordinances; national hate-crime statute.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Service refusal and facility ejection have no state-level remedy; exposure shifts with pending rulings.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower: no Visitor Conduct Register or blanket trans entry bar. Refusal is conditional on document/sex discrepancy, fraud findings require four elements plus waiver, and there are no daily check-ins, hotel reporting, or state tracking. Border discretion is real, but the usual consequence is exclusion, not administrative control of the entire stay.

Broadly similar: universal document scrutiny, documented arrest/detention, service and care refusal, and thin remedies mirror that anchor's biometric-checkpoint regime. Ours adds a criminal facility statute with birth-sex custody placement and a hostile supreme court, but scores upward on near-baseline violence, 67-68% public support for protections, and active litigation.

Lower than 0.55-B: that anchor is administrative - secondary screening, refused entry, slow appeals. This dossier adds criminal trespass exposure for facility use, a documented arrest ending in a men's ward, a statutory service-refusal right, and an 8-1 hostile high court, so severity after outing exceeds administrative denial.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a conditional but real border gate: mismatched documents trigger refusal and possible fraud referral, which is why eight governments issued advisories. Inside the division, facility access by gender identity is barred in public buildings, backed by a trespass offence requiring departure on request - one documented arrest ended with 24 hours in a men's ward, showing birth-sex custody operates. The religious-liberties statute plus absent state nondiscrimination law means service refusal has no local remedy. Detention escalates into national custody exposure (conversion-therapy policy, documented immigration abuse). Offsetting these, society polls majority-supportive, bias killing is near baseline with successful federal prosecution, and litigation keeps changing which national orders bind. Severity if outed is mostly ejection, arrest, or entry refusal - not imprisonment or death.
